title: Driver roster
context: Fleet ops wants a clean roster of every driver grouped by market.
task: List each driver's name, city and vehicle_type, arranged by city and then by name within each city.
hint: No filter needed — pick the three columns, then choose sort keys so the list is stable, with a second key to break ties.
answer: SELECT name, city, vehicle_type FROM drivers ORDER BY city, name;

title: Rides that actually ran
context: Revenue reporting counts only trips that finished, never cancellations.
task: Return ride_id, fare and distance_km for rides that were completed.
hint: The lifecycle of a ride is recorded in a status column — keep only the finished ones (text values go in single quotes).
answer: SELECT ride_id, fare, distance_km FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed';

title: Rides priced during surge
context: Pricing wants to see which trips were charged above the normal rate.
task: Return ride_id, surge_multiplier and fare for rides that were charged at a surge rate rather than the standard one.
hint: A multiplier of 1 means no surge — you want the ones charged more than that.
answer: SELECT ride_id, surge_multiplier, fare FROM rides WHERE surge_multiplier > 1;

title: Top drivers in one city
context: A 'best of Bengaluru' promo features highly rated local drivers.
task: Return name and rating for Bengaluru drivers whose rating is at least 4.7.
hint: Two things must both be true — the right city and a high enough rating.
answer: SELECT name, rating FROM drivers WHERE city = 'Bengaluru' AND rating >= 4.7;

title: Low-cost fleet
context: The budget fleet is made up of autos and motorbikes.
task: Return name and vehicle_type for drivers who drive either an Auto or a Moto.
hint: The vehicle has to be one of a short list of values.
answer: SELECT name, vehicle_type FROM drivers WHERE vehicle_type IN ('Auto','Moto');

title: Everything that didn't finish
context: Support reviews every trip that ended in something other than a completed ride.
task: Return ride_id and status for rides that did not complete.
hint: You want every row except the ones matching a single value.
answer: SELECT ride_id, status FROM rides WHERE status <> 'completed';

title: Mid-distance trips
context: A pricing study focuses on typical city hops between 5 and 10 km.
task: Return ride_id and distance_km for rides that ran from 5 to 10 km inclusive.
hint: An inclusive range on distance covers both endpoints in one condition.
answer: SELECT ride_id, distance_km FROM rides WHERE distance_km BETWEEN 5 AND 10;

title: 8 a.m. pickups
context: Demand analysts are isolating the morning rush at eight o'clock.
task: Return ride_id and pickup_time for rides picked up during the 8 a.m. hour, given pickup_time is stored as 'HH:MM' text.
hint: Match the beginning of the time text rather than comparing numbers.
answer: SELECT ride_id, pickup_time FROM rides WHERE pickup_time LIKE '08:%';

title: Trips with no trip time
context: A data check flags rides where no duration was ever recorded — typically cancellations.
task: Return ride_id and status for rides that have no recorded duration.
hint: A missing value isn't zero and isn't blank — test for the absence of a value.
answer: SELECT ride_id, status FROM rides WHERE duration_min IS NULL;

title: Longest trips
context: A leaderboard highlights the five longest rides taken.
task: Return ride_id and distance_km for the five longest rides, breaking ties by ride_id.
hint: Sort by distance from longest down, add a tiebreaker, then keep only the top few.
answer: SELECT ride_id, distance_km FROM rides ORDER BY distance_km DESC, ride_id LIMIT 5;

title: Newest drivers
context: Onboarding calls the most recently joined drivers to check in.
task: Return name and join_date for the three drivers who joined most recently.
hint: Sort by join date with the newest at the top, then cut the list short.
answer: SELECT name, join_date FROM drivers ORDER BY join_date DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Fare per kilometre
context: Unit economics needs the price of each completed trip per kilometre.
task: Return ride_id and the fare divided by distance (as fare_per_km, to 2 decimals) for completed rides that actually covered some distance.
hint: Compute a value from two columns and round it — and make sure you never divide by a zero distance.
answer: SELECT ride_id, ROUND(fare / distance_km, 2) AS fare_per_km FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' AND distance_km > 0;

title: What the driver keeps
context: Drivers take home 75% of the fare on every completed trip.
task: Return ride_id and the driver's share (as driver_take, to 2 decimals) — three-quarters of the fare — for completed rides.
hint: Scale the fare by the driver's share and round the result.
answer: SELECT ride_id, ROUND(fare * 0.75, 2) AS driver_take FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed';

title: Average trip speed
context: Ops wants the average speed of each completed trip in km/h.
task: Return ride_id and speed in km/h (as speed_kmh, to 1 decimal) for completed rides with a recorded duration, given distance is in km and duration is in minutes.
hint: Distance over time gives speed — but convert the minutes to hours first, and only include rides with a non-zero duration.
answer: SELECT ride_id, ROUND(distance_km / (duration_min / 60.0), 1) AS speed_kmh FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' AND duration_min > 0;

title: Hour of pickup
context: Demand analysis needs the pickup hour as a number it can group on.
task: Return ride_id and the pickup hour as an integer (as pickup_hour), pulled from the 'HH:MM' pickup_time text.
hint: Take the first part of the time text and turn it into a number.
answer: SELECT ride_id, CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS pickup_hour FROM rides;

title: Driver first names
context: The app greets drivers by first name only.
task: Return driver_id and just the first name (as first_name) — the part of name before the first space.
hint: Find where the first space sits, then take the text up to it.
answer: SELECT driver_id, SUBSTR(name, 1, INSTR(name, ' ') - 1) AS first_name FROM drivers;

title: Rides by outcome
context: The trip funnel shows how rides split across completed, cancelled and no-show.
task: Return each status and the number of rides (as rides) that ended with it.
hint: Collapse the rides to one row per status and count how many fall into each.
answer: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides GROUP BY status;

title: How many riders are active?
context: Growth wants the count of riders who have taken at least one trip, not the number of trips.
task: Return active_riders: the number of different riders who appear in the rides table.
hint: A rider can appear on many rides — make sure each one is counted only once.
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rider_id) AS active_riders FROM rides;

title: Gross bookings
context: Finance reports gross bookings as the total fare of trips that completed.
task: Return gross_bookings: the total fare across completed rides, to 2 decimals.
hint: Add up the fares, but only over the rides that finished.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(fare), 2) AS gross_bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed';

title: Typical fare and trip length
context: Two headline averages sit at the top of the rides dashboard.
task: Return avg_fare and avg_km (both to 2 decimals) across completed rides, in a single row.
hint: Two averages side by side, taken over the finished rides only.
answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(fare), 2) AS avg_fare, ROUND(AVG(distance_km), 2) AS avg_km FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed';

title: Service quality by market
context: Regional managers compare the typical driver rating across their cities.
task: Return each city and the average driver rating (as avg_rating, to 2 decimals) in that city.
hint: Average the rating within each city — one row per market.
answer: SELECT city, ROUND(AVG(rating), 2) AS avg_rating FROM drivers GROUP BY city;

title: Fare range
context: Pricing wants the cheapest and priciest completed trip on record.
task: Return min_fare and max_fare among completed rides, in a single row.
hint: The lowest and the highest fare, reported together over finished rides.
answer: SELECT MIN(fare) AS min_fare, MAX(fare) AS max_fare FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed';

title: Fleet mix
context: Supply planning wants to know how the fleet breaks down by vehicle.
task: Return each vehicle_type and the number of drivers (as drivers) in it.
hint: One row per vehicle type, counting the drivers in each.
answer: SELECT vehicle_type, COUNT(*) AS drivers FROM drivers GROUP BY vehicle_type;

title: Riders by market
context: The demand team sizes the rider base in each city.
task: Return each city and the number of riders (as riders) based there.
hint: Collapse riders to one row per city and count them.
answer: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS riders FROM riders GROUP BY city;

title: Bookings per driver
context: Driver payouts start from each driver's total completed fare.
task: Return driver_id and total completed fare (as bookings, to 2 decimals) for each driver.
hint: Keep the finished rides, then total the fare within each driver.
answer: SELECT driver_id, ROUND(SUM(fare), 2) AS bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id;

title: Supply hours per driver
context: Ops tracks how many hours each driver spent online.
task: Return driver_id and total online hours (as hours, to 1 decimal) for each driver, from the shift log.
hint: Add up the online hours per driver — the data lives in the shifts table.
answer: SELECT driver_id, ROUND(SUM(hours_online), 1) AS hours FROM driver_shifts GROUP BY driver_id;

title: Busiest pickup hours
context: Marketplace planning wants to know when demand peaks during the day.
task: Return the pickup hour (as pickup_hour, an integer) and ride count (as rides) for the five busiest hours, most rides first and hour as a tiebreaker.
hint: Derive the hour from the time text, count rides in each, then rank and keep the top few.
answer: SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS pickup_hour, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides GROUP BY pickup_hour ORDER BY rides DESC, pickup_hour LIMIT 5;

title: Power riders
context: A loyalty tier is aimed at riders who take a lot of trips.
task: Return rider_id and ride count (as rides) for riders with more than 10 rides of any status.
hint: Group by rider and count, then keep only groups whose count clears the threshold — a filter on the grouped result, not on individual rows.
answer: SELECT rider_id, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides GROUP BY rider_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 10;

title: Readable trip log
context: A trip log should show the driver's name instead of an ID.
task: Return ride_id, the driver's name (as driver) and fare for every ride.
hint: The name lives on the drivers table — connect each ride to its driver.
answer: SELECT r.ride_id, d.name AS driver, r.fare FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id;

title: Premier trips
context: A premium report covers completed trips taken in Premier vehicles.
task: Return ride_id and fare for completed rides where the driver's vehicle is a Premier.
hint: Vehicle type sits on the driver, not the ride — join to it, then filter on both the vehicle and the ride's outcome.
answer: SELECT r.ride_id, r.fare FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE d.vehicle_type = 'Premier' AND r.status = 'completed';

title: Bookings by city
context: Leadership wants completed bookings totalled by the driver's home city.
task: Return each city and its total completed fare (as bookings, to 2 decimals), where the city comes from the driver.
hint: City lives on the drivers table — join to it, keep finished rides, and total the fare per city.
answer: SELECT d.city, ROUND(SUM(r.fare), 2) AS bookings FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.city;

title: Tips per driver
context: Drivers want to see the tips they've earned across their trips.
task: Return driver_id and total tips (as tips) for each driver, where tips are recorded against rides.
hint: Tips sit on the ratings table but the driver sits on the ride — link them, then total tips per driver.
answer: SELECT r.driver_id, SUM(rr.tip) AS tips FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id GROUP BY r.driver_id;

title: Distance band
context: Trips are bucketed into short, medium and long for a distribution chart.
task: Return ride_id and a band that reads 'Long' for rides of 15 km or more, 'Medium' for 5 km or more, and 'Short' otherwise.
hint: Test the thresholds in order from the largest down, so each ride lands in exactly one band.
answer: SELECT ride_id, CASE WHEN distance_km >= 15 THEN 'Long' WHEN distance_km >= 5 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Short' END AS band FROM rides;

title: Monthly ride volume
context: A trend line shows how ride volume moves month over month.
task: Return the month as YYYY-MM and the ride count (as rides) for each month, in chronological order.
hint: Reduce each ride_date to its year-and-month, group on that, and sort the months in order.
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', ride_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;
